name: Event Organization Portal - SIA Project 21 22
description:
Information Systems - academic year 21/22
Course Project
Version 1.0.1 - 20/12/2021
Consider the following scenario:

A startup intends to develop a web portal that can help people who intend to organize an event, bringing together in a single website the information concerning the guests and the various services necessary for the event itself to take place.

The platform to be developed envisages the presence of providers and guests, in addition to the organizer.

At registration, providers supply, in addition to their credentials, their personal data and the data of the company they manage (VAT number, company address, accepted payment methods).

The provider, once registered, will be able to enter the services offered by their company, each belonging to a category (catering, hairdresser, florist etc.), each of which will be associated with a virtual showcase in which the provider can upload demonstration photos, together with the corresponding prices and the hours corresponding to the particular service shown by the showcase (e.g. Hairdresser's blow-dry service has as hours 10:00-12:00 from Tuesday to Thursday, Haircut + shampoo service with hours 8:00-12:00 + 15:00-18:00 from Tuesday to Saturday).

The event organizer, identified by their tax code, at registration, in addition to choosing their credentials, will provide their personal data, residence data and their IBAN for the possible payment of the services.

The organizer, through the portal, will be able to create the event, choosing the type of event (wedding, graduation, concert…) to organize, the date, the place where it will be held and the budget planned for the organization of the event. When creating the event the organizer will be able to choose from a pre-existing list the types of service for which they are interested in receiving help (for example catering, flowers, taxi service etc.).

The organizer will also be able to add the guests to the portal, entering the corresponding data, specifying, in addition to the personal data, the email with which the guest will be identified (and which they will use to log in) and the category to which the guest belongs (relative, friend, colleague etc.).

For each guest added, the system will generate an invitation code that will be sent by email to the specified address; this code will be used by the guest as a password to access the portal.

The organizer will also have available a blog associated with their event in which the organizer or the guests can write information about the event, post photos or videos and leave their thoughts by creating new posts or commenting on the existing ones.

The organizer, once the event has been created, will be able to view, for each service chosen when creating the event, the showcases of the providers that supply the chosen type of service and to arrange an appointment compatible with the hours observed by that service, specifying the details and any special requests. The provider, through their interface, will be able to view the various appointment requests and will have to approve them. The approved requests are displayed directly in a calendar on the site associated with the event, where the organizer will be able to consult the appointments for the agreed services.

After the meeting between the provider and the organizer (in which they agree on the details of the service), the provider calculates the quotation and proceeds to upload the amount on the portal, associating it with the completed appointment.

Once the upload has taken place the organizer can choose whether to accept or reject the quotation; if it is accepted, the total amount is subtracted from the remaining budget. By accepting the amount, the organizer chooses the payment mode (instalments, deposit + balance or full amount) and the payment method (online or on site). If the payment takes place on site the provider will proceed to confirm the amount paid through the portal (in the case of payment in several instalments the provider confirms the amount of each instalment received).

At any time the organizer will be able to consult the history of the contracts (with the related status and cost) and the budget balance for the entire event.
highLevelGoals: The Event Organizer aims to use the portal to define event details such as type, date, location, and budget, and to select desired service categories.
The Event Organizer seeks to add guest details, generate invitation codes, and manage guest access to the event portal and associated blog.
The Event Organizer wants to browse provider showcases, arrange appointments for services, and manage service agreements and quotations.
The Event Organizer needs to accept or reject quotations, manage payment modes and methods, and track the event budget and contract history.
The Event Organizer desires a platform to share information, photos, and videos, and to interact with guests through posts and comments.
The Provider aims to create a profile, provide company and personal data, and upload service details with demonstration photos, prices, and availability.
The Provider seeks to view and approve appointment requests from organizers, calculate and upload quotations, and confirm payments received.
The Guest wants to log in using an invitation code, view event details, and participate in the event blog by creating posts or commenting.
lowLevelGoals: The Event Organizer can initiate the creation of a new event within the portal, providing essential details such as the event's category, scheduled date, and geographical location.
The Event Organizer can define and modify the financial budget allocated for a specific event, ensuring financial planning and control.
The Event Organizer can browse and choose from a predefined list of service categories relevant to their event, such as catering, entertainment, or venue.
The Event Organizer can input and store information for each guest invited to an event, including names and contact details.
The Event Organizer can trigger the system to create distinct, secure invitation codes for each guest, enabling controlled access to event resources.
The Event Organizer can configure and modify the level of access guests have to different sections and features of the event portal.
The Event Organizer can control which guests are able to view, post, or comment on the event's dedicated blog.
The Event Organizer can search and filter available service providers by specific categories to find suitable options for their event.
The Event Organizer can send a formal request to a chosen provider to schedule a meeting or consultation regarding their services.
The Event Organizer can access, review, and track the status of formal agreements made with service providers.
The Event Organizer can receive, review, and organize price quotations submitted by various service providers.
The Event Organizer can formally approve a received quotation from a provider, indicating their agreement to proceed with the service at the quoted price.
The Event Organizer can formally decline a received quotation from a provider, indicating their decision not to proceed with the service at the quoted price.
The Event Organizer can choose and set up various payment options (e.g., credit card, bank transfer) for their event's financial transactions.
The Event Organizer can view real-time updates and summaries of their event's financial expenditures against the allocated budget.
The Event Organizer can access a chronological record of all contracts and agreements related to their event.
The Event Organizer can compose and publish new content, including text, on the event's dedicated blog.
The Event Organizer can add image files to their blog posts to enhance visual communication with guests.
The Event Organizer can embed or upload video files into their blog posts to share dynamic content with guests.
The Event Organizer can review, approve, or delete comments made by guests on their blog posts.
The Provider can initiate the creation of their professional profile within the portal, providing essential identification details.
The Provider can enter and update information related to their company, such as business name, registration details, and contact information.
The Provider can enter and update personal information, such as their name, contact details, and professional credentials.
The Provider can add comprehensive information about the services they offer, categorizing them appropriately for discoverability.
The Provider can add image files to visually represent and showcase the quality and nature of their services.
The Provider can define and update the cost associated with each of their services, including different pricing models or packages.
The Provider can manage their calendar and indicate when their services are available for booking by event organizers.
The Provider can access a list of all pending requests for appointments from event organizers.
The Provider can formally accept an appointment request, confirming their availability and commitment to the meeting.
The Provider can use the system to determine and create a detailed price quotation for services requested by an event organizer.
The Provider can submit the calculated quotation to the event organizer through the portal for their review.
The Provider can mark a payment as received within the system, updating the financial status of a service agreement.
The Guest can gain access to the event-specific portal by entering a unique code provided by the event organizer.
The Guest can access and review all relevant information about the event, such as schedule, location, and other important announcements.
The Guest can compose and publish their own content on the event's blog, subject to organizer permissions.
The Guest can respond to and interact with content published by the organizer or other guests on the event blog.
